# Tensile test results

## Method

Stress was regressed on strain using ordinary least squares, with an intercept, over the full measured strain range (0.0002–0.0020). The slope is the estimated elastic modulus; because stress is in MPa and strain is dimensionless, slopes are reported in MPa and GPa. Material fits pool the three specimens (30 measurements per material). Specimen-to-specimen spread is summarized as the sample standard deviation of the three individual specimen slopes.

## Results

| Material | Pooled modulus (GPa) | R² | Mean specimen modulus ± SD (GPa) | Specimen range (GPa) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Aluminum | 69.38 | 0.99834 | 69.38 ± 1.76 | 67.38–70.64 |
| Steel | 199.06 | 0.99844 | 199.06 ± 2.00 | 197.28–201.22 |
| Titanium | 116.56 | 0.99788 | 116.56 ± 1.71 | 114.62–117.83 |

## Figure

![Stress-strain measurements and pooled linear fits](stress_strain_fits.svg)

## Interpretation

The pooled linear fits give the estimated elastic moduli shown above. All fits are strongly linear over the measured interval, while the specimen-level spread reflects variation among the three tested specimens. These are full-range linear estimates; if the strain interval includes yielding or other nonlinear behavior, a fit restricted to the initial elastic segment would be more appropriate. The data provided do not identify a narrower elastic-only interval.

item.text:
The fitted moduli are **69.38 GPa for aluminum**, **199.06 GPa for steel**, and **116.56 GPa for titanium**. The pooled fits have R² values above 0.997.

I saved the write-up and figure as [results.md](/private/tmp/tmps33d5_b0/pete/projects/elastic-modulus/results.md) and [stress_strain_fits.svg](/private/tmp/tmps33d5_b0/pete/projects/elastic-modulus/stress_strain_fits.svg). The analysis script is [analyze.py](/private/tmp/tmps33d5_b0/pete/projects/elastic-modulus/analyze.py).

The estimates fit the full measured strain range. If that range includes nonlinear or yielding behavior, a fit over the initial elastic segment could give a different modulus.
